A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 26-page versions of the same paper, including Appendices A–G. Text comparison and page rendering support reliable comparison of the equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v4 reports original experiments on fictitious, continual, and real-world unlearning in Section 5, with additional experiments, ablations, and generated examples in Appendices E–G.

after.justification: v5 retains the original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendices E–G, including TOFU evaluations, real-world unlearning, ablations, and generated examples.

M1.justification: The proposed ME+GD and IDK+AP procedures in Sections 3–4 are unchanged. The corrected baseline equations align with descriptions already present in v4; they do not establish a changed algorithm or training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same TOFU tasks and continual scenarios, real-world individuals, Alpaca supplementation, and five downstream benchmarks. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main and appendix experiments. Section 2.3 corrects equations for existing NPO, GD, and KL components without reporting a different evaluated comparator or procedure.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendices D–E retain the same data splits, model configurations, metrics, training schedules, sample sizes, LoRA settings, and evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: The regularization variants, longer-training analysis, unlearning-strength sensitivity, question-masking ablation, continual-unlearning failure analyses, LoRA experiments, and Forget Quality case studies are all retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix F retains the same KS-test-based Forget Quality analysis and p-values. No repeated-run information, seed reporting, confidence intervals, or statistical estimation practices are added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted trends, rankings, and generated examples match throughout both PDFs. For example, Table 2 retains ME+GD Model Utility of 0.4901 and Forget Efficacy of 0.9312; appendix results also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2.3 corrects NPO's expectation in Eq. (2) from the retain set D_R to the forget set D_F, and GD/KL expectations in Eqs. (4)–(5) from D_F to D_R. These repair mathematical loss definitions to match the existing prose. The derivations in Appendices B–C are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: additional output metrics, analysis of targeted and untargeted unlearning, and the ME and AP approaches. No core claim is strengthened, narrowed, or added.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning hallucinations, excessive ignorance, shrinking retain sets, NPO reference-model failures, and limitations of Forget Quality remain unchanged in Sections 3–5 and Appendix F.

D1.justification: Appendix D and Section E.8 retain identical hardware, optimization, hyperparameter, checkpoint, and LoRA details. Code and data access information is unchanged; the equation corrections introduce no new implementation disclosures.

R1.justification: Section 6, the in-text citations, and the reference list are unchanged. No cited work or substantive positioning relative to earlier research is added, removed, or revised.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v4, dated 21 May 2025, to v5, dated 10 August 2025. Prose, terminology, section structure, and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–12 and Tables 1–14 retain their structure, captions, axes, legends, and placement. The equation corrections and version-stamp update do not reorganize the document's layout.

improvement.justification: v5 fixes three inconsistent sampling domains in Section 2.3, making the loss equations agree with the forget/retain roles already described in v4. This improves mathematical accuracy and reduces implementation ambiguity. The proposed methods, empirical evidence, claims, and appendix analyses remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
